title: アルゴリズムとデータ構造
subtitle: Algorithms and Data Structure
educationalGoal:
In order to develop good programs, knowledge about data structures and algorithms is necessary. The objectives of this course are the following:
1. Learning fundamental knowledge about data structures and algorithms.
2. Developing data structure and algorithm selection skills suitable for the problems.
advice:
A data structure is a form in which data is stored in a computer, and an algorithm is a "procedure used to solve a problem" that abstracts a program. In order to write a good program, a good data structure and a good algorithm are necessary. Since multiple data structures and algorithms can be used to solve a problem, students of this course will learn about time complexity, which is a typical index for comparing them. They will also compare multiple algorithms with varying time complexities in these lessons.

The order of the learning contents shown in the lesson schedule is a guideline. Students should follow the instructions of the teacher in charge for additional details. At a minimum, the following contents will be addressed: sort algorithms (basic and advanced techniques, including merge sort and quick sort), basic data structures (array, list, stack, queue, tree, and graph), and search algorithms on graph. Other contents may be added.
books: 「アルゴリズムとデータ構造」（第2版）森北出版株式会社
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge about inequality, polynomial functions, exponential functions, logarithm functions, numerical sequences, and recurrence relation.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand several data structures.
Be able to understand several algorithms.
Be able to judge algorithms from the viewpoint of computational complexity.
Be able to select the best algorithm and best data structure for a given problem.

achievementLevels.ideal:
Be able to explain the algorithms and data structure required for efficient data rearrangement and conduct searches perfectly.
Be able to evaluate the computational complexity of each algorithm logically.
achievementLevels.standard:
Be able to explain the concrete behavior of the algorithms and data structure required for efficient data rearrangement and searching.
Be able to evaluate the computational complexity of each algorithm approximately.
